correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier scalar-amplitude identity and character second moment imply the uniform error bound using the proved pointwise nonlinear-phase estimate. In the connected witness family the exceptional Fourier-character event has probability \(h^{-1}\); its normalized signed-binomial sum converges to a Gaussian, inducing a nonconstant cubic phase. The coin component transverse to the uniform coin is \(O(h^{-1})\), so the full measured-position probability has precisely the claimed leading deficit. Endpoint modes, all degrees and time-parity constraints are covered. Direct evolution and finite binomial recomputation are supporting checks, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The precise worst-case failure rate is operationally important to parity-timed one-shot transport. The theorem closes an explicit convergence-rate question raised by the motivating work, identifies the sharp universal exponent, and explains why atypically structured connected graphs incur a cubic-Gaussian transfer deficit. The exponent and construction distinguish unrestricted cubelike graphs from the much better-behaved hypercube; neither an arbitrary slice nor a mere renamed identity.
